subject: ArborHealth renewal — executive approval needed for save package
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: ArborHealth renewal at risk — proposed save package

Team,

Quick summary: ArborHealth (enterprise, production, heavy embeddings + chat) notified renewals team this morning that they are evaluating a competitor. Usage is steady but the C-level contact cited unit economics and an upcoming multi-region rollout as reasons to press for better pricing and an SLA commitment.

They signed in 2024 at $1.2M ARR; renewal is due 12/15. Current ask from procurement (attached) is:
- 30% discount first year (aggressive)
- Reset to 12-month term starting at renewal (they want to move billing cadence)
- 99.99% SLA with 30% service credit for breaches

What I recommend as a save package (to present to execs):
- 15% renewable discount year 1 (with programmatic step-down to 10% year 2)
- $75k one-time credit applied to invoice 1
- Term reset to 12 months but add a 6-month early-exit right for Redwood if we see sustained cost beyond forecast (protects us)
- SLA: keep current SLA language; offer a capped operational credit arrangement (max 3 months of credits over contract life) and a 30-day remediation window before credits apply

Attachments: ArborHealth_Renewal_Usage.pdf (usage/seat breakdown), Save_Package_Pricing.xlsx (proposed math)

As this exceeds standard delegation (discount > 10% + one-time credits), Marcus — can you add the formal request to deal desk and route to Vivek for sign-off? Vivek — we need executive authority by EOD to get a counter in front of ArborHealth next week.

Thanks,
Laura
--
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: ArborHealth renewal at risk — proposed save package

Vivek / Neha / Laura,

I logged this as a non-standard concessions request in the deal desk tracker (RDW-1729). Key inputs:
- Baseline ARR: $1.2M
- Forecasted 2027 consumption: $1.35M (they expand regionally)
- Margin stress if we go >18% discount or open-ended SLA credits

Requested approvals:
1) Approve up to 15% ACV discount year 1 (with 10% floor year 2)
2) Approve $75k one-time credit
3) Allow term reset to 12 months with the proposed early-exit protection for Redwood
4) SLA: Approve capped credit framework (not to exceed 3 months equivalent) and require remediation window

If we approve, I will:
- Finalize counter language (legal-reviewed template)
- Prepare a DocuSign envelope for the commercial terms
- Coordinate with Finance to ensure revenue recognition treatment for the credit

Quick note on alternatives: we can reduce discount to 12% and add a usage-based true-up at 6 months to protect margin. If you want that, I can model it.

Marcus
--
Marcus Lin
Director, Deal Desk
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 18:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Approve conditional save package for ArborHealth (RDW-1729)

Thanks for the package and the modelling. I reviewed RDW-1729 and will approve the following, on a conditional basis:

- Approve 15% discount Year 1 (10% Year 2 floor)
- Approve $75k one-time credit (applied to invoice 1)
- Approve term reset to 12 months with Redwood early-exit clause as drafted
- Approve SLA credit framework with the cap Marcus proposed (max 3 months equivalent credits over the term)

Conditions before signature:
1) CFO (finance@redwoodinference.com) must sign off on the credit/recognition treatment — Marcus, please confirm impact to recognized revenue schedule.
2) Legal must run a final pass on the SLA language to ensure we have explicit remediation steps and a mutual force majeure carve-out for region outages.
3) Customer must sign the counter by 12/01 to allow us time to onboard multi-region nodes for their rollout.

I am authorizing the sales team to present this counter to ArborHealth. If they push for a deeper discount (>20%) or an uncapped SLA credit, we stop and escalate to the CEO.

Vivek
--
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Commercial
vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
From: Jared Mills <jared.mills@arborhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ArborHealth Procurement <procurement@arborhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: ArborHealth renewal — executive approval needed for save package

Laura / Neha,

Thanks — we appreciate the fast follow. The team reviewed your proposed counter and is generally aligned. A couple of asks before we execute:
- Please confirm the credit application timing (need assurance it hits invoice dated renewal start)
- We prefer the SLA to be 99.99% given our regulatory posture; would Redwood consider 99.99% if we accept a phased increase (99.9% in Q1, 99.99% after multi-region rollout confirmed)?

We are ready to move quickly; if you can send a DocuSign-ready counter with the agreed one-time credit and the phased SLA approach, we can get sign-off from our CFO by next week.

Jared
--
Jared Mills
Head of Cloud Procurement
ArborHealth
jared.mills@arborhealth.com
